app.name: AgenticTeam
app.summary: A portable AI delivery organization: 50 role definitions, shared protocols and skills that one stdlib Python CLI compiles into each coding harness's native format, plus a run-state machine and supervisor that hold agents to evidence and human gates.

stack.choice: Python standard library only, no third-party packages
GitHub Actions job matrix on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS

approach.layout: Flat Python repository. scripts/agentic_team.py is both the harness compiler and the single writer of run state; roles, protocols, skills, templates and seed knowledge are Markdown and JSON sources it installs into target projects. team.json is the one manifest everything else is checked against.
approach.notes: This plan maps main's working tree as it stands, including untracked plan and prompt files. Generated outputs are checked, never hand-edited. Claude Code and Codex both work in this repository (AGENTS.md); implementation work goes on task branches merged into autonomy-integration, so files that exist only there are not in this map.

patterns.purpose: One role definition per agent in team.json, grouped by department folder
patterns.instance: agents/<department>/<id>.md with frontmatter `name` (equal to the file stem and the team.json id) and `description` (at most 300 characters, with a trigger clause such as 'Use when...' or 'Activate when...' and an exclusion clause 'Not for ... (use <id>)'). Core roles follow the shape of agents/engineering/fullstack-engineer.md (## Mission, ## Expertise, ## Operating protocol, ## Collaboration, ## Skills you lean on, ## Guardrails, ## Self-learning, ## Output contract). Specialists use exactly ## When, ## Inputs, ## Procedure, ## Output, ## Done when, ## Hand-offs, ## Access in that order, as in agents/specialists/sre-engineer.md. The roster lint also requires: a compiled prompt of 400 to 2500 tokens; none of the retired terms it bans (task board, task evidence record, status.md, plan.md, qa.md, lessons.md, decisions.md, hardening, wcag 2.1, phase gate, '## standing orders', 'phase <n>', 'ship phase'); exactly one **Owns:** line across all roles for each lifecycle artifact, with fixed owners (ceo: BRIEF.md, ASSUMPTIONS.md, DELIVERY-REPORT.md; product-manager: PRD.md; cto-architect: ARCHITECTURE.md; ux-ui-designer: DESIGN.md; delivery-lead: READINESS.md, RETROSPECTIVE.md; qa-lead: VERIFICATION.md; release-manager: RELEASE.md; cmo: MARKETING.md), and no **Owns:** line in read-only or research roles; and only known role ids in backticks. A new role also needs its team.json entry (with activate_when for a specialist), the README counts, roster.json in team.json order, a guide rebuild, and regenerated golden files if it is in helpers.GOLDEN_ROSTER. Department folders: leadership, engineering, support, marketing, specialists.

One Markdown protocol linked from runtime/templates/router.md or protocols/agent-contract.md (an unlinked protocol is never read by an agent). It names sibling protocols by bare filename and installed paths as .agentic-team/..., and is scanned for retired vocabulary (test_law) and overclaims (test_release).

patterns.purpose: Templates the runtime copies into a run's stages
patterns.instance: One Markdown template, filled in one of five ways, so check which before editing. (1) Artifact templates registered in ARTIFACT_TEMPLATES (assumptions, brief, delivery-report, prd, readiness, release, retrospective, risks, verification) are copied by `scaffold`, which replaces only `{{project}}`. (2) task.md, stage-context.md, fusion-brief.md, fusion-proposal.md and fusion-critique.md are filled with str.format: use `{field}` names and double any literal brace. (3) fusion-dissent.md has `{{council}}` replaced. (4) fusion-synthesis.md and fusion-decision.md are copied as they are. (5) adr.md, checkpoint.md and handoff.md are forms agents copy by hand, referenced from protocols/communication.md and the agentic-build skill. router.md is installed verbatim as .agentic-team/AGENTS.md. Every template must be referenced from the CLI or from shared law (test_law).

patterns.purpose: Entry file of each installed skill
patterns.instance: skills/<name>/SKILL.md with frontmatter `name` equal to the folder (lowercase words joined by hyphens), `description` longer than 80 and at most 1024 characters, and `compatibility` (required, at most 500 characters). The body is a runbook with exact `.agentic-team/bin/agentic_team.py` commands and no TODO. Every skill folder also needs agents/openai.yaml. Only folders belong directly under skills/: a stray file there breaks the skill checks and ships into every install (D11). A skill that a workflow runs also needs team.json workflows.<id>.skill set to skills/<name>.

patterns.purpose: Codex/OpenAI interface metadata for each skill
patterns.instance: YAML with interface.display_name, interface.short_description, interface.default_prompt (which must contain `$<skill-name>`) and policy.allow_implicit_invocation; copy skills/agentic-build/agents/openai.yaml. policy.allow_implicit_invocation is optional; the three shipped skills that set it set false.

patterns.purpose: Supporting reference each skill loads on demand
patterns.instance: One Markdown reference that its SKILL.md links to; scanned for retired vocabulary like all shared law.

knowledge/playbooks/<role-id>.md created from _template.md, headed `# Playbook — <role-id>`, with checks under ## Before starting, ## While building and ## Before claiming done. Seeded checks end with `<!-- status: baseline -->`. Lines an agent adds use the candidate form from knowledge/playbooks/README.md: `- [ ] <imperative check>  <!-- status: candidate · learned: YYYY-MM-DD · source: <run>/<task> · cost: <what it broke> -->`. Promoting a candidate to baseline is the owner's decision (protocols/evolution.md). About forty lines at most.

patterns.purpose: One unittest module per area of the system
patterns.instance: A unittest module that imports from helpers (`import helpers` or `from helpers import ...`) before anything uses the CLI, because that import isolates AGENTIC_TEAM_HOME. It uses helpers.team, helpers.fresh_project() and helpers.run_cli() instead of the real home or source tree, and reads expected values from team.json or config/ instead of literal counts (several existing tests still hard-code them, GAP-1). New shared fixtures go in helpers.py; test_installers reuses shells() from test_repairs_packets.

patterns.purpose: Expected compiler output per harness, compared byte for byte
patterns.instance: Never written by hand. After a compiler change, regenerate with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_safety_net.py"` (PowerShell: `$env:UPDATE_GOLDEN=1; python -m unittest ...`; cmd: `set UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 && python -m unittest ...`) and review the diff; the role set is fixed in helpers.GOLDEN_ROSTER. Files under nested .claude/, .codex/ and .agentic-team/ folders are invisible to this blueprint (D6).

A JSON object with name, description and steps (optional harness and preset), using only the step forms documented at the top of evals/run_scenarios.py (cli, human, write, state, task, exec_py, python). Together the scenario names must cover greenfield, plan-given, brownfield, fusion, rejection and self-approval (test_evals). File names use snake_case (plan_given.json); the `name` field uses kebab-case (plan-given-hitl-bmad) and is what the coverage check matches.

roster.role: Owner. Holds the constitution (roles, protocols, policy, manifest), legal files, and every final approval
Code lane: CLI and supervisor, installers, tools, tests, evals, run templates, skills, schemas and CI
Docs lane: user docs, plans, prompt packs, progress records, seed knowledge and the shared guide

decisions.decision: Phase P1 maps the system as it stands on main instead of a walking skeleton.
decisions.why: This is an existing codebase; later phases come from the owner's next body of work.

decisions.decision: Every verify command calls python, never python3.
decisions.why: On Windows python3 resolves to the Microsoft Store stub, and verify runs through cmd.exe here. verify also runs through cmd.exe, where `bash` is the WSL launcher, so no check in this plan calls bash directly; tests/test_installers.py finds Git Bash itself.

decisions.decision: The paid live smoke eval is never a verify command; evals/live_smoke.py is verified by its offline scoring tests.
decisions.why: Running it spends model credits.

decisions.decision: Generated outputs (the guide's index.html and agent-roster.csv; the generated sections of docs/cli.md and docs/architecture.md) are verified by their --check commands and never edited by hand.
decisions.why: They are rebuilt from data and the CLI parser; hand edits are overwritten.

decisions.decision: Python 3.10 stays in the CI matrix and as the installer minimum for now; flagged for the owner.
decisions.why: Python 3.10 reached end of life on 2026-10-01 (devguide.python.org/versions), but the code deliberately supports it (tomllib imports are guarded).

decisions.decision: Golden fixtures under nested harness folders (tests/golden/<harness>/.claude/, .codex/ and .agentic-team/) are not tracked here: 28 of the 48 golden files are.
decisions.why: The tool's built-in ignore list matches .claude/, .codex/ and .agentic-team/ at any depth, and ignore[] cannot remove defaults. The hidden files stay covered by tests/test_safety_net.py GoldenSnapshotTests. Reported to the skill's learning loop.

decisions.decision: Ownership runs in three lanes: the owner holds the constitution, Claude Code the code, Codex the docs.
decisions.why: The owner's choice. Git history showed no existing split, so lanes are set by kind of work.

decisions.decision: team.json, LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md belong to the owner, not to a lane.
decisions.why: team.json sets each role's access class and tier, and protocols/evolution.md reserves permission changes to the human owner; the other two are legal.

decisions.decision: The guide's shared files (progress.json, updates.json, documents.json, index.html, agent-roster.csv) are owned by codex under the /docs/ rule, and Claude Code also updates them through the UPDATING.md steps. The tool allows one owner per path, so this cannot be encoded as co-ownership: Claude Code runs the shared-roster step with BLUEPRINT_OWNER unset, which turns off the owner check for every path during that step (the guard still refuses unplanned files). Keeping to those five files during the step is Claude Code's responsibility. GAP-12 records the structural fix.
decisions.why: The owner chose to share these files with Claude Code, which AGENTS.md requires after every finished task.

decisions.decision: Regenerating the generated sections of docs/cli.md and docs/architecture.md (agentic_team.py docs --write) is an expected Claude Code edit inside the docs lane.
decisions.why: Those sections are rendered from the CLI parser and config/guarantees.json, which live in other lanes.

decisions.decision: Do not run `blueprint.py contracts --write` in this repository.
decisions.why: It writes skills/README.md, which breaks test_law (it treats every entry under skills/ as a skill folder) and would ship into every install.

decisions.decision: P1 changes no file. It is done when `verify --run --phase P1` passes; until then status --next lists files as open because they are unverified.
decisions.why: This is a map of an existing system, not a build.

decisions.decision: The installers are verified by tests/test_installers.py: install.sh into a temporary project for every harness in team.json through a real bash (Git Bash on Windows), install.ps1 through PowerShell, and install.sh's LF line endings. .gitattributes keeps *.sh at LF. These changes are uncommitted until the owner approves a commit; on HEAD 9f863f7 the installer and .gitattributes checks fail.
decisions.why: No test executed either installer, and a CRLF checkout made bash reject install.sh with a syntax error.

decisions.decision: The docs and repo modules have no default check. Every file names a test that reads it; files no test reads get a content check that states exactly what it asserts.
decisions.why: A module default made 20 files count as verified by commands that never opened them.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: Tests hard-code counts and versions (50 roles and 18 specialists in test_runtime, 7 gates in test_law with a keyword map in test_runtime, "3.0.0" in test_release), so a role, gate or version change needs a test edit in another lane.
decisions.why: Read them from team.json and config/ instead.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: config/policies.json and config/guarantees.json have no JSON Schema, and team.schema.json leaves harnesses, workflows and model_profiles as bare objects. team.schema.json also declares pattern, minItems and uniqueItems constraints that schema_problems never checks.
decisions.why: Their shapes live only in the CLI and the tests.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: Nothing validates a run's state.json against schemas/run-state.schema.json; the schema is documentation only. The schema is also out of date: init_run writes budgets, event_count, events_head and run_uid, which it does not list.
decisions.why: Validate written state with the same subset approach validate uses for team.json, or retire the schema.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: docs/agent-team-guide/build.py --check needs a local autonomy-integration branch whose head matches progress.json runtimeIntegration, so it fails on a fresh clone, never runs in CI, and goes stale when that branch moves.
decisions.why: It is the guide module's check, not part of the P1 exit.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: The generated sections of docs/cli.md and docs/architecture.md live inside hand-written files in another lane (D10).
decisions.why: Moving them to their own files would give them one owner.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: team.yaml is read by no code; only README links to it.
decisions.why: Delete it with the link, or record the release that removes it.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: roster.json repeats team.json fields that build.py overwrites, and build.py hard-codes "All 13 compiler targets".
decisions.why: Keep only guide-specific fields and derive the count.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: One role change touches three lanes: the role file and team.json (owner), tests and golden files (Claude Code), README counts, roster.json and the guide (Codex); every constitution change also needs a CHANGELOG.md line in Codex's lane.
decisions.why: Recorded so the cost is visible; the lanes were the owner's choice.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: ci.yml jobs that use secrets and can spend model credits (ocr-review, live-smoke) sit in the code lane.
decisions.why: They run only when the owner sets a repository variable.

decisions.decision: Run verify on Python 3.12 or later.
decisions.why: On Python 3.10 and 3.11, unittest exits 0 when -p matches no file, so a missing test file would pass its check; 3.12 and later exit 5.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: config/guarantees.json (owner) names test classes in tests/ (Claude Code), so renaming a test breaks the owner's ledger.
decisions.why: Rename tests only together with the ledger row, in one change the owner approves.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: A release bump and a new gate each need edits in all three lanes at once: VERSION and the test_release literal (Claude Code), the config files, guardrails.md and agent-contract.md (owner), router.md and the gate keyword maps (Claude Code), and the CHANGELOG (Codex). Every lane's check stays red until all land.
decisions.why: Do them as one coordinated change; fixing GAP-1 removes the test edits.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: The tool has no co-ownership, so the shared guide files rely on D9's discipline. Splitting updates.json into one file per agent that build.py merges would remove the conflict.
decisions.why: Repo change, not made by this plan.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: The review recommended giving runtime/templates/router.md and schemas/team.schema.json (they restate the gates and define the access and tier values) and knowledge/playbooks/ and knowledge/evolution/ (baseline checks ship to every install; the changelog records constitution changes) to the owner.
decisions.why: The owner kept them in their lanes on 2026-11-06.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: Three docs currently fail the shared doc tests: docs/design-review-plan.md links protocols/design-review.md, which exists only on autonomy-integration (untracked file); docs/durable-core-prompt.md line 45 parses as an unknown command (uncommitted edit); docs/autonomy-progress-review.md links into a removed local worktree (committed on main, so it also fails on a fresh clone and in CI).
decisions.why: Codex fixes them in the docs lane; until then 23 files stay unverified.

decisions.decision: Known gap, not fixed by this plan: The P1 exit's preflight step only reports: preflight_skills.py exits 0 unless --require names a missing skill.
decisions.why: Kept as a report so the exit does not depend on optional skills installed on one machine.
